WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): identity from the JWT, never from the request body: the gate's ELEVEN attribution-pin checks - a spoofed auth_uid/worker_name/submitted_by/registrant/completer/author_name on an INSERT is server-pinned to the caller across logbook, asset_nodes, projects, pm_assets, pm_completions, community_posts, community_replies, inventory_items, engineering_calcs, parts_records and voice_journal_entries - plus audit_actor_bind, where a client-forged hive_audit_log.actor is overwritten with the caller's real identity. Persona under test on this row: two_context (foreign XP log unreachable) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.
evidence.value_checked: hive isolation gate: 26 pass / 0 fail, live two-tenant, rolled back, role+claims correct

findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 1 of its 1 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - achievement_xp_log (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 4 read relation(s), 1 were probed live at the gateway (achievement_xp_log).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

Achievements carry their criteria as an instruction rather than a description - 'Reach Level 50 in any 5 domains to unlock' sits on the tile it governs, so a person reads WHAT TO DO, not merely what they lack. evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK. The oracle asks that XP per action be stated BEFORE the action, since that is the only point at which it can motivate. Eight came from a regex over award_achievement_xp calls in every trg_%achievement_xp function; three more (logbook_submit, logbook_close, community_post) pass a VARIABLE rather than a literal and were invisible to that regex, so they were read from the function bodies directly - which is also where the conditional bonuses and their exact triggering conditions came from, so the published bonus text states what actually earns it. findings.title: TRACED: the .wh-avatar overflow is the avatar's OWN centred text, not the level badge - and it is a consequence of this session's overflow:visible fix
findings.detail: THREE PROBES, AND THE FIRST TWO WERE WRONG - recording the chain because the wrong answers were the plausible ones. (1) I assumed the badge: .wh-avatar-lvl is positioned bottom:-8px to hang below the circle and the avatar had overflow:hidden, so the two rules fought. That WAS a real defect - 21% of every level pill clipped across 32 avatars, digits cut - and fixing it (mask moved to .wh-avatar > img, container set to overflow:visible) was correct and is verified: 0 pills clipped on community and achievements. (2) I then assumed the badge also explained the horizontal scrollWidth excess and widened my probe's absolute-child exclusion to DESCENDANTS. That made the readings WORSE - community 14 -> 22, achievements 11 -> 20 - because the badge is centred with translateX(-50%) and never passes the avatar's right edge: measured layout box right edge 61 against clientWidth 64 (3px INSIDE), painted box right edge 48. I reverted it rather than add a third guess. (3) THE DECISIVE TEST, which should have been first: remove the suspect and see if the symptom goes. Hiding the pill, removing only its transform, and pulling it fully inside vertically ALL left scrollWidth 84 against clientWidth 64 - a 20px excess completely unchanged in every case. So the badge contributes nothing to it. THE ACTUAL CAUSE: .wh-avatar is `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center` with its initials as a direct text node. A centred flex item wider than its container overflows EQUALLY ON BOTH SIDES, so text ~104px wide in a 64px content box spills ~20px each way and scrollWidth reads 64 + 20 = 84 - which is exactly the measurement. The excess is the avatar's own label being wider than the circle. AND THIS IS A SIDE EFFECT OF MY OWN FIX, stated plainly rather than left for someone to find: under the previous overflow:hidden those oversized initials were CLIPPED to the circle; under overflow:visible they now SPILL outside it. Both the badge and the text were sharing one overflow property for opposite purposes, and no single value satisfies both. TO CLOSE, and it needs a look at the rendering rather than another measurement: identify which avatars actually carry oversized labels (the sample here shows initials like 'PA' fitting and glyph labels like the star tier badges running wide), then constrain the LABEL - a max-width with a smaller font-size or a single-glyph cap - so the text fits the circle while the badge keeps hanging below it. Constraining the text is the fix; putting the clip back would re-break the badge.
findings.observed: avatar clientWidth 64 / scrollWidth 84 / excess 20, unchanged with the pill hidden, un-transformed, or moved inside; pill layout right edge 61 vs clientWidth 64

findings.title: RESOLVED - NOT A DEFECT: the .wh-avatar overflow is a decorative spinning tier halo drawn by a PSEUDO-ELEMENT, structurally invisible to any DOM walk
findings.detail: FOUR PROBES, AND THE FIRST THREE WERE WRONG. Recording the whole chain because the wrong answers were each more plausible than the right one, and the shape of the error is the lesson. GUESS 1 - the level badge. .wh-avatar-lvl is positioned bottom:-8px to hang below the circle while the avatar had overflow:hidden, so the two rules fought. That WAS a real defect and the fix stands, verified: 21% of every level pill had been clipped across 32 avatars, and 0 are clipped now. But it did not explain the horizontal excess. GUESS 2 - the badge again, via my probe. I widened the absolute-child exclusion to DESCENDANTS to absorb it, and the readings got WORSE: community 14 -> 22, achievements 11 -> 20. Measured, the badge's layout box ends at 61 against clientWidth 64 - three pixels INSIDE - and its painted box at 48. Reverted. GUESS 3 - the avatar's own centred text. .wh-avatar is display:flex with justify-content:center, and a centred flex item wider than its box overflows equally BOTH ways, which would make scrollWidth = clientWidth + 2x the spill. Arithmetically perfect and factually wrong: the initials 'PA' measure 21px in a 64px box via a Range, and 0 of 20 avatars have text wider than their container. THE DECISIVE TEST, which should have been probe 1: remove the suspect and re-read. Hiding the pill, removing its transform, and pulling it inside all left the excess UNCHANGED at 20px - so the badge was exonerated by measurement long before I stopped blaming it. Then, forcing `content: none` on both pseudo-elements took scrollWidth from 91 to EXACTLY 64 = clientWidth. THE CAUSE: .wh-tier-legend::after is an 84x84 ring at inset:-10px with animation wh-spin, plus a 72x72 ::before, on a 72px avatar - a decorative rotating halo marking the top tier. It is intentional, it is aria-invisible, and it is a PSEUDO-ELEMENT, so no querySelectorAll('*') walk can ever see it. That is why three rounds of DOM reasoning failed: I was looking for the contributor among elements, and the contributor is not an element. VERDICT: THERE IS NO OVERFLOW DEFECT ON THESE PAGES. evidence.asserts: every piece of edge-pinned chrome declares a safe-area inset for ITS OWN edge - read from the AUTHORED CSS over CDP (inline style, attribute style, and every matched rule), not from getComputedStyle, which flattens an unapplied env() to 0px and would report a missing declaration as satisfied
evidence.checked: 2026-08-20 gate:cj_safe_area - clean full run: 22 pages, every edge-pinned element resolved, decoration and modal overlays excluded and COUNTED as skips rather than silently dropped
evidence.value_checked:
the direction is part of the claim: top-pinned chrome needs inset-top, bottom-pinned needs inset-bottom, so a direction-blind match cannot pass this. Falsifiable by a planted bottom-pinned element with no inset (caught as uncovered) beside one carrying env(safe-area-inset-bottom) (correctly clean) - and the satisfier proves the CDP path really does see an inline env(), which it must, since coverage reads inlineStyle.cssText first
 | depends_on: tools/prove_safe_area.mjs

scenarios.question: layout under real content at three VERIFIED widths - innerWidth, never the requested viewport
scenarios.oracle: at a VERIFIED innerWidth of ~390 nothing overflows its container and the document does not scroll sideways

evidence.asserts: no element on the populated page overflows the viewport horizontally without an ancestor that clips it - measured at the width the browser ACTUALLY reports (innerWidth is verified, not assumed from the requested viewport), and an ancestor with overflow-x hidden/clip is recorded as clipping rather than counted as a defect
evidence.checked: 2026-08-20 gate:cj_viewport_overflow - clean full run: 22 pages x 3 verified widths (390/641/1280), 0 with an UNCLIPPED overflow, 0 unverifiable, scale 1
evidence.value_checked:
0 unclipped of 22 pages x 3 widths - and the instrument is FALSIFIABLE: --teeth plants a 400px-wide box at left:100% plus a 40px box inside the viewport, and requires the violator caught and the satisfier clean. The expectation is COMPUTED at inject time by walking the same ancestor rule the prover uses, because on a page whose BODY clips x the violator correctly lands in offenders and NOT in unclipped - asserting a fixed outcome there would red a correct instrument (hive clips at BODY, and the teeth pass reported exactly that)
 | depends_on: tools/prove_viewport_overflow.mjs

scenarios.question: every component's induced states - loading, skeleton, disabled, busy, populated - distinguishable and honest
scenarios.oracle: the component's loading state is distinguishable from its empty state

evidence.asserts: the component reaches a settled, populated state - no node is left in a permanent loading or skeleton shimmer, and the states the page announces during load (skeleton, aria-busy, disabled) are the ones it actually uses
evidence.checked: 2026-08-20 gate:ck_component_states - clean full run: 22 pages, controlFailed [] and stuck [], measured with a MutationObserver armed from the FIRST MUTATION rather than after settle
evidence.value_checked:
0 stuck of 22 pages, and the detector is proven live on EVERY page rather than by a separate mode: the prover APPENDS a real skeleton node (class 'skeleton wh-control-probe') and asserts the observer count ROSE (controlCaught: after > before), enforcing it under --gate via results.filter(r => r.controlCaught !== true). So a page reporting 0 skeletons has PROVEN it can see one. Measuring after settle is how 'this page has no loading state' gets recorded for a page that paints nine skeleton rows during load - hive did exactly that, and a candidate now counts as a skeleton only at placeholder GEOMETRY (>=24px both axes, or an explicit skeleton/shimmer class), because an 8px dot is a status light and a 648x260 block is a skeleton
 | depends_on: tools/prove_component_states.mjs

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (30 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it. tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs graded 36 of 43 registry targets with ZERO failing, and its summary line reads 'every focusable control shows a causally-verified focus indicator'. On this view that sentence is true the way any statement about an empty set is true: the report records focus.candidates = 0 and focus.checked = 0. No focusable control was examined, so nothing about focus indication was established. Banking it green would put a row in the bank whose evidence is an empty denominator - the exact false green this bank exists to prevent. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW, NOT A DEFECT. Six of the thirty-six graded views hold no focusable controls at all - engineering-design's guide tab, shift-brain's verdict summary and its details disclosure, report-sender's contacts list, public-feed's feed list, achievements' recent list. They are READ surfaces: text, cards and figures. A view with nothing to focus cannot fail a focus oracle, and it cannot pass one either. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE SIBLING ORACLES, because they are NOT vacuous here: this same run measured accessible names and reduced-motion on the same views and those are real readings - a name applies to any control, focusable or not, and 'nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion' is a statement about the whole subtree. So the a11y run is only empty for FOCUS on these six. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS ROW: either the view genuinely gains an interactive control (then re-run and grade it), or the row is dispositioned declared-na with this reason under R10 - which needs a replacement oracle named, and the honest replacement is that the view is READABLE and its figures are labelled (CL contrast + CM what_is_this_number), not that its focus ring works. AND AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, since the prover is otherwise strong: its per-view PASS does not distinguish 'checked N controls, all good' from 'checked none'. The distinction is recoverable only from focus.candidates in the report, so a consumer that reads the exit code alone would bank all six of these as proven. The count belongs in the printed line.

evidence.asserts: the bulk condition this oracle names - enough rows that the surface must page or virtualise - does not exist for this subject, so there is no second page on which a row could appear twice
evidence.checked: Measured live rather than assumed, on both sides: what the surface RENDERS and what its reads ASK FOR. the achievements grid holds 6 achievements for this worker, and the page renders 10 entries in #recent-list with NO pager control. Its reads are 'achievement_xp_log order=earned_at.desc,id.asc limit=30' and 'agent_followups order=due_at.asc,id.asc limit=5'. NO PAGER CONTROL IS PRESENT on this subject, which is the correct outcome for a collection that fits in one request rather than a missing affordance. WHAT IS PROVEN ANYWAY, so this is not a hidden risk: every ordered read on this page carries a UNIQUE TIEBREAKER as its last sort key - id.asc - so equal values on the primary sort column have a defined relative order and a keyset cursor could not skip or repeat a row if the volume ever grew. The mechanism the oracle cares about is verified on the wire; only the multi-page TRAVERSAL is unexercised, and it cannot be exercised without 50 rows existing. findings.detail: FAILS: with 11 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it shows only a GENERIC error ("Skip to main content ℹ Achievements failed to load.") - the person is told it broke, never that they are not allowed.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: a first run to value journey on this page, walked as this persona, reaches value without a dead end
evidence.checked: PASSES: reached value: 2470 chars, 18 actionable control(s), 0 stuck skeletons, 0 failed read(s). PERSONA: this row was walked as "worker (own progress)" (slot P1), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'worker'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. That distinction was learned by getting it wrong: clearing the hive key made asset-hub answer, entirely correctly, 'Asset Hub needs a hive ... Go to Hive', and the oracle called it a DEAD END for all three personas - including a supervisor who is demonstrably a member of hive 636cf7e8, which is the giveaway that indicted the probe rather than the page. Clearing the worker-name key likewise bounced signed-in people off achievements, report-sender and project-report. The journey under test is a first-time signed-in MEMBER, so membership and identity are as fixed as the session. NON-VACUITY: a journey that cannot be CONSTRUCTED fails - a page that will not load, or a persona that cannot be established, is a finding about the surface or about this harness's knowledge of it, never a quiet pass. This is the discipline the marketplace spec tests/ux-journeys.spec.ts already carries; this prover extends it to the 22 product pages rather than re-deriving it. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT, and the specific lie this oracle is built to refuse: A FIRST-RUN SCREEN CAN BE A LIE. This platform has already shipped a page (skillmatrix) that asked a worker to re-pick a discipline they had already chosen, because the READ had failed and the page rendered its first-run onboarding as the fallback. To a naive 'did the person reach something actionable?' check that scores as a PASS - there is content, there are buttons, there is a clear next step - while it is the OPPOSITE of value: it invites the person to redo setup they already did, and can overwrite it. So reaching an onboarding screen is credited as value ONLY if the page's own reads SUCCEEDED, counted from the network (4xx/5xx on /rest/v1, /rpc, /functions/v1), not guessed. Onboarding over a failed read is banked as a FAILURE with its status codes. That is the A16.P7 mechanism rule: credit the right cause, not merely the observed property. A dead end (<3 visible actionable controls, or <300 characters) fails. A still-shimmering VISIBLE skeleton after 7.6s fails - a page that never resolves is not value, and only visible skeletons count because a hidden template is not a state. For two_context, BOTH identities must reach value; one succeeding while the other dead-ends is a failure. J2 repeat_visit is measured as a DELTA, in the same session, where the only thing that changed is that the person has been here before. A page that demands setup on the RETURN which it did not demand on the first run is one finding; a page that demands it BOTH times is a different and lesser one, and the two are reported separately rather than flattened. 'Setup demanded' matches the page asking the person to choose or configure before it will show them anything (choose/select your discipline|trade|role|hive|shift, get started, set up your, complete your profile). J4 two_sided_same_object COMPARES TWO CONCURRENT SESSIONS OF THE SAME IDENTITY, and why it is not two ROLES is a finding in itself. The first version compared a worker's rendering against a supervisor's and reported logbook as '3 of 8 shared figures DISAGREE between two members of the same hive' - #total-count 314 vs 516, #open-count 2 vs 6. Every number was correct: the page deliberately scopes the whole view by role, and the giveaway was a THIRD element - #lb-progress read 'JOBS CLOSED' for the worker and 'TEAM JOBS' for the supervisor. Those are answers to different questions that happen to share an element id, so calling them a contradiction would have banked findings alleging the platform disagrees with itself while it was scoping correctly. Matching on the adjacent label did not rescue it either: #total-count is labelled 'entries' on BOTH sides, and only that other element disclosed the scope - itself a real gap, recorded against CM what_is_this_number rather than smuggled in here. So the second side is the SAME identity in a second session, which is what these pages' own anatomy means by two_context ('two workers, one entry'); role scoping is then identical by construction, and any remaining disagreement is genuine - a race, or a stale cache. Figures are keyed by ELEMENT ID plus the page's own LABEL for that figure (aria-label, else the surrounding card text with the value removed). An id present for only one session is SKIPPED, not failed, because that is authorisation working. A comparison over ZERO shared figures is reported as NOT MEASURED and FAILS - zero disagreements over zero comparisons is not a pass. J5 abandon_resume TYPES INTO A COMPOSER AND WALKS AWAY - the most ordinary thing a person on a plant floor does, because they get called away mid-entry. A marker string is typed into the first visible text field of the page's own dialog (opened via tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the SAME grounded table four other provers read, so this cannot drift from how those views are known to open), the walker then leaves the page entirely and returns. THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES IT FAIR: a preserved DRAFT is good UX, not a defect, so the marker is looked for in two places that mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD = a draft was kept, which PASSES and is noted as deliberate. Out in the page's own CONTENT = it HALF-LANDED, and a person who typed and walked away now holds a record they never submitted. NOTHING IS EVER SUBMITTED, so this stays non-writing: the marker only ever reaches an input's value. COVERAGE IS HONEST: 16 drivable composers exist across 11 of the 22 pages. findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: a repeat visit journey on this page, walked as this persona, does not make a returning person redo setup

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state

On this page the person-caused action is nothing at all - its XP and badges are awarded server-side by triggers and RPCs - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: a first run to value journey on this page, walked as this persona, reaches value without a dead end
evidence.checked: PASSES: redirected to "index" — the expected auth wall for an anon persona on a private page, and it offers 65 actionable control(s). No claim is made about achievements's own content, which this persona never sees.. PERSONA: this row was walked as "anon (public profile view)" (slot P2), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'anon'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. That distinction was learned by getting it wrong: clearing the hive key made asset-hub answer, entirely correctly, 'Asset Hub needs a hive ... Go to Hive', and the oracle called it a DEAD END for all three personas - including a supervisor who is demonstrably a member of hive 636cf7e8, which is the giveaway that indicted the probe rather than the page. Clearing the worker-name key likewise bounced signed-in people off achievements, report-sender and project-report. The journey under test is a first-time signed-in MEMBER, so membership and identity are as fixed as the session. NON-VACUITY: a journey that cannot be CONSTRUCTED fails - a page that will not load, or a persona that cannot be established, is a finding about the surface or about this harness's knowledge of it, never a quiet pass. This is the discipline the marketplace spec tests/ux-journeys.spec.ts already carries; this prover extends it to the 22 product pages rather than re-deriving it. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT, and the specific lie this oracle is built to refuse: A FIRST-RUN SCREEN CAN BE A LIE. This platform has already shipped a page (skillmatrix) that asked a worker to re-pick a discipline they had already chosen, because the READ had failed and the page rendered its first-run onboarding as the fallback. To a naive 'did the person reach something actionable?' check that scores as a PASS - there is content, there are buttons, there is a clear next step - while it is the OPPOSITE of value: it invites the person to redo setup they already did, and can overwrite it. So reaching an onboarding screen is credited as value ONLY if the page's own reads SUCCEEDED, counted from the network (4xx/5xx on /rest/v1, /rpc, /functions/v1), not guessed. Onboarding over a failed read is banked as a FAILURE with its status codes. That is the A16.P7 mechanism rule: credit the right cause, not merely the observed property. A dead end (<3 visible actionable controls, or <300 characters) fails. A still-shimmering VISIBLE skeleton after 7.6s fails - a page that never resolves is not value, and only visible skeletons count because a hidden template is not a state. For two_context, BOTH identities must reach value; one succeeding while the other dead-ends is a failure. J2 repeat_visit is measured as a DELTA, in the same session, where the only thing that changed is that the person has been here before. A page that demands setup on the RETURN which it did not demand on the first run is one finding; a page that demands it BOTH times is a different and lesser one, and the two are reported separately rather than flattened. 'Setup demanded' matches the page asking the person to choose or configure before it will show them anything (choose/select your discipline|trade|role|hive|shift, get started, set up your, complete your profile). J4 two_sided_same_object COMPARES TWO CONCURRENT SESSIONS OF THE SAME IDENTITY, and why it is not two ROLES is a finding in itself. The first version compared a worker's rendering against a supervisor's and reported logbook as '3 of 8 shared figures DISAGREE between two members of the same hive' - #total-count 314 vs 516, #open-count 2 vs 6. Every number was correct: the page deliberately scopes the whole view by role, and the giveaway was a THIRD element - #lb-progress read 'JOBS CLOSED' for the worker and 'TEAM JOBS' for the supervisor. Those are answers to different questions that happen to share an element id, so calling them a contradiction would have banked findings alleging the platform disagrees with itself while it was scoping correctly. Matching on the adjacent label did not rescue it either: #total-count is labelled 'entries' on BOTH sides, and only that other element disclosed the scope - itself a real gap, recorded against CM what_is_this_number rather than smuggled in here. So the second side is the SAME identity in a second session, which is what these pages' own anatomy means by two_context ('two workers, one entry'); role scoping is then identical by construction, and any remaining disagreement is genuine - a race, or a stale cache. Figures are keyed by ELEMENT ID plus the page's own LABEL for that figure (aria-label, else the surrounding card text with the value removed). An id present for only one session is SKIPPED, not failed, because that is authorisation working. A comparison over ZERO shared figures is reported as NOT MEASURED and FAILS - zero disagreements over zero comparisons is not a pass. J5 abandon_resume TYPES INTO A COMPOSER AND WALKS AWAY - the most ordinary thing a person on a plant floor does, because they get called away mid-entry. A marker string is typed into the first visible text field of the page's own dialog (opened via tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the SAME grounded table four other provers read, so this cannot drift from how those views are known to open), the walker then leaves the page entirely and returns. THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES IT FAIR: a preserved DRAFT is good UX, not a defect, so the marker is looked for in two places that mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD = a draft was kept, which PASSES and is noted as deliberate. Out in the page's own CONTENT = it HALF-LANDED, and a person who typed and walked away now holds a record they never submitted. NOTHING IS EVER SUBMITTED, so this stays non-writing: the marker only ever reaches an input's value. COVERAGE IS HONEST: 16 drivable composers exist across 11 of the 22 pages. A page with no composer is left OWED, never failed - 'this surface has nothing to abandon' is a design fact about a read-only page, and manufacturing a red for it is the vacuity R10 exists to forbid. J3 cross_surface_handoff FOLLOWS A REAL LINK OUT, and its claim is deliberately NARROW because a wide one would be dishonest: most in-app links carry no parameter, so there is no 'context' to survive, and asserting that there is would be inventing a property in order to measure it. What is actually checked: (1) the handoff LANDS WHERE THE LINK PROMISED - the href's page is the page reached, so a link that silently bounces elsewhere via an auth wall or redirect has broken the handoff even though it appeared to work; (2) the destination is NOT A DEAD END, on the same rule and the same reasoned-empty exemption J1 uses, so handing off into a well-explained empty state passes and handing off into a blank does not; and (3) IF the link carries a query parameter, the destination must REFLECT it rather than drop it - the only case where 'context survived' is a real checkable claim, and it is checked. A page with no visible in-app link to another product page is left OWED, never failed. SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this row claims exactly ONE of J1 first_run_to_value, J2 repeat_visit or J4 two_sided_same_object, J5 abandon_resume or J3 cross_surface_handoff - one row, one claim, and the others are NOT settled by it. J4 compares two sessions of ONE identity, so it neither claims nor tests cross-ROLE agreement: a supervisor and a worker legitimately see differently scoped figures here. The failed-read tooth above is ARMED but not INDUCED here: this walk exercises a HEALTHY system, so a page passing J1 has not been shown to survive a refused read - inducing that is the CC failure-injection family's job, and a page can pass here and still fail there. NON-WRITING: nothing is typed or submitted; storage is cleared only inside a throwaway context that is closed after each persona.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA WITH A NAMED REPLACEMENT (rail R10), AND THE REASON IS THE ORACLE'S OWN WORD: MIDWAY. This oracle asks what happens when someone abandons PART-WAY THROUGH. On this page the person-caused action is nothing at all - its XP and badges are awarded server-side by triggers and RPCs - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-achievements-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: a repeat visit journey on this page, walked as this persona, does not make a returning person redo setup
evidence.checked: PASSES: returning person goes straight to content: 2432 chars, 17 control(s), no setup demanded. PERSONA: this row was walked as "two_context" (slot P3), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'two_context'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. That distinction was learned by getting it wrong: clearing the hive key made asset-hub answer, entirely correctly, 'Asset Hub needs a hive ... Go to Hive', and the oracle called it a DEAD END for all three personas - including a supervisor who is demonstrably a member of hive 636cf7e8, which is the giveaway that indicted the probe rather than the page. Clearing the worker-name key likewise bounced signed-in people off achievements, report-sender and project-report. The journey under test is a first-time signed-in MEMBER, so membership and identity are as fixed as the session. NON-VACUITY: a journey that cannot be CONSTRUCTED fails - a page that will not load, or a persona that cannot be established, is a finding about the surface or about this harness's knowledge of it, never a quiet pass. This is the discipline the marketplace spec tests/ux-journeys.spec.ts already carries; this prover extends it to the 22 product pages rather than re-deriving it. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT, and the specific lie this oracle is built to refuse: A FIRST-RUN SCREEN CAN BE A LIE. This platform has already shipped a page (skillmatrix) that asked a worker to re-pick a discipline they had already chosen, because the READ had failed and the page rendered its first-run onboarding as the fallback. To a naive 'did the person reach something actionable?' check that scores as a PASS - there is content, there are buttons, there is a clear next step - while it is the OPPOSITE of value: it invites the person to redo setup they already did, and can overwrite it. So reaching an onboarding screen is credited as value ONLY if the page's own reads SUCCEEDED, counted from the network (4xx/5xx on /rest/v1, /rpc, /functions/v1), not guessed. Onboarding over a failed read is banked as a FAILURE with its status codes. That is the A16.P7 mechanism rule: credit the right cause, not merely the observed property. A dead end (<3 visible actionable controls, or <300 characters) fails. A still-shimmering VISIBLE skeleton after 7.6s fails - a page that never resolves is not value, and only visible skeletons count because a hidden template is not a state. For two_context, BOTH identities must reach value; one succeeding while the other dead-ends is a failure. J2 repeat_visit is measured as a DELTA, in the same session, where the only thing that changed is that the person has been here before. A page that demands setup on the RETURN which it did not demand on the first run is one finding; a page that demands it BOTH times is a different and lesser one, and the two are reported separately rather than flattened. 'Setup demanded' matches the page asking the person to choose or configure before it will show them anything (choose/select your discipline|trade|role|hive|shift, get started, set up your, complete your profile). J4 two_sided_same_object COMPARES TWO CONCURRENT SESSIONS OF THE SAME IDENTITY, and why it is not two ROLES is a finding in itself. The first version compared a worker's rendering against a supervisor's and reported logbook as '3 of 8 shared figures DISAGREE between two members of the same hive' - #total-count 314 vs 516, #open-count 2 vs 6. Every number was correct: the page deliberately scopes the whole view by role, and the giveaway was a THIRD element - #lb-progress read 'JOBS CLOSED' for the worker and 'TEAM JOBS' for the supervisor. Those are answers to different questions that happen to share an element id, so calling them a contradiction would have banked findings alleging the platform disagrees with itself while it was scoping correctly. Matching on the adjacent label did not rescue it either: #total-count is labelled 'entries' on BOTH sides, and only that other element disclosed the scope - itself a real gap, recorded against CM what_is_this_number rather than smuggled in here. So the second side is the SAME identity in a second session, which is what these pages' own anatomy means by two_context ('two workers, one entry'); role scoping is then identical by construction, and any remaining disagreement is genuine - a race, or a stale cache. Figures are keyed by ELEMENT ID plus the page's own LABEL for that figure (aria-label, else the surrounding card text with the value removed). An id present for only one session is SKIPPED, not failed, because that is authorisation working. A comparison over ZERO shared figures is reported as NOT MEASURED and FAILS - zero disagreements over zero comparisons is not a pass. J5 abandon_resume TYPES INTO A COMPOSER AND WALKS AWAY - the most ordinary thing a person on a plant floor does, because they get called away mid-entry. A marker string is typed into the first visible text field of the page's own dialog (opened via tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the SAME grounded table four other provers read, so this cannot drift from how those views are known to open), the walker then leaves the page entirely and returns. THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES IT FAIR: a preserved DRAFT is good UX, not a defect, so the marker is looked for in two places that mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD = a draft was kept, which PASSES and is noted as deliberate. Out in the page's own CONTENT = it HALF-LANDED, and a person who typed and walked away now holds a record they never submitted. NOTHING IS EVER SUBMITTED, so this stays non-writing: the marker only ever reaches an input's value. COVERAGE IS HONEST: 16 drivable composers exist across 11 of the 22 pages. A page with no composer is left OWED, never failed - 'this surface has nothing to abandon' is a design fact about a read-only page, and manufacturing a red for it is the vacuity R10 exists to forbid. J3 cross_surface_handoff FOLLOWS A REAL LINK OUT, and its claim is deliberately NARROW because a wide one would be dishonest: most in-app links carry no parameter, so there is no 'context' to survive, and asserting that there is would be inventing a property in order to measure it. What is actually checked: (1) the handoff LANDS WHERE THE LINK PROMISED - the href's page is the page reached, so a link that silently bounces elsewhere via an auth wall or redirect has broken the handoff even though it appeared to work; (2) the destination is NOT A DEAD END, on the same rule and the same reasoned-empty exemption J1 uses, so handing off into a well-explained empty state passes and handing off into a blank does not; and (3) IF the link carries a query parameter, the destination must REFLECT it rather than drop it - the only case where 'context survived' is a real checkable claim, and it is checked. A page with no visible in-app link to another product page is left OWED, never failed. SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this row claims exactly ONE of J1 first_run_to_value, J2 repeat_visit or J4 two_sided_same_object, J5 abandon_resume or J3 cross_surface_handoff - one row, one claim, and the others are NOT settled by it. J4 compares two sessions of ONE identity, so it neither claims nor tests cross-ROLE agreement: a supervisor and a worker legitimately see differently scoped figures here. The failed-read tooth above is ARMED but not INDUCED here: this walk exercises a HEALTHY system, so a page passing J1 has not been shown to survive a refused read - inducing that is the CC failure-injection family's job, and a page can pass here and still fail there. NON-WRITING: nothing is typed or submitted; storage is cleared only inside a throwaway context that is closed after each persona.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. findings.detail: FAILS: UNEXPLAINED — still renders 6 of 9 number(s) non-zero (5 of them also present signed-in, which may be static furniture: 18 .wh-avatar-lvl; 38 .wh-avatar-lvl; 63 .wh-avatar-lvl) and nothing on screen says the data could not be loaded. With a session this view rendered 14 non-zero value(s) over 2429 characters; with the auth token removed from storage it rendered 6 over 1698, and the page did not redirect, did not add a sign-in prompt it was not already showing, and did not state that anything failed to load. What is on screen after the kill: "Skip to main content Growth ← Skills Achievements Live · refreshed on load · Based on your achievements, XP history & worker · XP this week: points earned in the last 7 d".  WHY THIS FINDING IS WORDED NARROWLY, and what it deliberately does NOT claim: the obvious reading - 'the page should have redirected or announced an ended session' - is WRONG on this platform, and checking that is what kept this row honest. index.html:3520 shows a designed branch for 'Guest worker (has name, no auth session)' which shows an upgrade nudge, and index.html:902-906 stamps its wh-signed-in paint-hint from wh_last_worker + wh_active_hive_id in localStorage precisely so a known user does not watch the marketing landing collapse into the dashboard (a measured CLS of 0.24). So a cached identity with no session is a SUPPORTED state here, not a defect, and demanding a redirect would have manufactured one. What is not defensible is the other half: hive-scoped reads that could not have succeeded rendering as zeros with nothing saying so. On index that surfaces as the words 'ALL CLEAR - Nothing urgent right now' beside the real hive name - an affirmative safety claim derived from a read that never happened, which is the same shape as the two moderation badges that asserted '0 waiting' on a failed read. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, live, and what the oracle deliberately is NOT: it is not 'does the page redirect to sign-in'. Several of these surfaces are legitimately readable signed-out, so a redirect is only ONE honest answer and demanding it would manufacture defects on the public pages. The oracle is the NEGATIVE: a page must never present a signed-out state as though it were signed-in data. Three behaviours are accepted and the row NAMES which one this page did - (1) redirect to a sign-in surface or render a sign-in prompt it was not rendering before, (2) render an empty state that STATES its reason, (3) be a genuinely public surface that renders identical content either way. What FAILS is the fourth: hive-scoped numbers still on screen, or bare zeros and dashes with no explanation, standing in for a read that could not have succeeded. THE SESSION IS KILLED IN localStorage, NOT IN COOKIES, and that detail is the difference between a real measurement and a vacuous one: supabase-js persists the session as sb-<project-ref>-auth-token in localStorage, so clearing cookies would leave the page fully signed in and the probe would measure nothing while reporting a pass. Every sb-* / auth-token / supabase key in BOTH localStorage and sessionStorage is swept (hardcoding one project ref is the other way this goes silently vacuous), then the page is RELOADED so the client re-reads storage from cold. THE CONTROL IS THE SIGNED-IN READING, TAKEN FIRST: the same page is measured with a session, and the two readings must differ. A probe that cannot prove it changed anything cannot report that the change was handled correctly - so a page that looks identical either way is either genuinely public (case 3, and then it must show no hive-scoped values at all) or the kill did not take, and those two are never allowed to be confused: the second is recorded UNGRADED, never as a pass. TWO FALSE READINGS WERE CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, and both are why this row is trustworthy. FIRST, THE PROVER REPORTED A PASS OVER AN EMPTY DENOMINATOR: the text-matching regexes were declared in Node scope but referenced inside the page.evaluate callback, which runs in the BROWSER, so every page threw ReferenceError and came back UNGRADED - and the summary printed 'PASS - no page presents a dead session as signed-in data', true only in the sense that no page had been looked at. Zero failures over zero measurements is now an explicit FAIL, louder than a real failure, because a failure gets triaged while a vacuous green gets banked. SECOND, A BODY-WIDE KEYWORD MATCH READ THE PAGE'S OWN MARKETING COPY AS EVIDENCE: public-feed was credited with 'says-signed-out' because its text matched /sign in/ - but it matched BEFORE the kill too, since the page permanently renders 'Sign In ->' and 'Sign in to join the conversation' as its read-only CTA, and its body was byte-identical either way at 2438 characters with zero non-zero values both times. A signed-out sentence now only counts if it APPEARED after the kill, and the unchanged/public case is tested BEFORE any text match rather than after it - which is how public-feed came to be recorded as what it actually is, a public surface, rather than as a page that announced a dead session. THIRD, A LEAK SUB-CHECK WAS BUILT AND THEN DELIBERATELY DEMOTED TO INFORMATIONAL, because it could not tell leaked USER data from static FURNITURE and it got that wrong in BOTH directions. Comparing the signed-in and signed-out readings for values that survived, it called index a leak on a bare '3' with no class - a coincidence between a step indicator and a tile - and then, after being tightened to require a class and more than one digit, it called achievements a leak on 18/38/63/83 .wh-avatar-lvl, which are the Iron/Bronze/Silver/Gold tier THRESHOLDS: identical for every user and CORRECT to survive a signed-out reload. Telling those apart requires knowing which numbers are user-scoped, which no generic DOM read can answer, so claiming it anyway would be manufacturing findings. The oracle now grades ONLY the classification it can actually establish, and the survivor list travels with the row as context for a human rather than as a verdict. FOURTH, THE FAILING VERDICT MISDESCRIBED ITS OWN MEASUREMENT: it read 'N number(s), all zero/blank' on every page that reached that branch, while achievements had 6 of 9 non-zero. A verdict that contradicts its own reading is the mislabelled-metric defect wearing a test's clothes; it now states the counts it measured. FIFTH, A PAGE STILL LOADING WAS BEING REPORTED AS A PAGE THAT FAILED TO EXPLAIN ITSELF. The sweep called asset-hub, analytics and shift-brain UNEXPLAINED EMPTY with ZERO numbers on screen - but zero numbers is equally the signature of a page that had not finished rendering 3.4 seconds after a reload, which is the SLOW-vs-STUCK distinction the component-states prover already had to learn. A page that looks under-rendered, or is still showing aria-busy / skeleton / spinner elements, now gets another 6 seconds and is re-read; if it is still unsettled the row is UNGRADED rather than failed, because the reading genuinely cannot tell the two apart. SIXTH, THE ORACLE WAS FAILING PAGES THAT HAVE NO SUBJECT. assistant and report-sender rendered ZERO non-zero values even WITH a session - a chat thread and an empty report list - so there is no figure on either page that a dead session could turn into a false reassurance. Failing them would be asserting a defect in the absence of the thing the assertion is about, so a page with no data signed-in is now UNGRADED with that reason recorded. Across six corrections the pattern is the same one this whole bank keeps teaching: the instrument was wrong more often than the pages were, and every one of these was caught by reading what the page actually rendered instead of trusting the verdict. SEVENTH, THE READINESS GUARD ITSELF WAS TOO BLUNT AND DISQUALIFIED FINISHED PAGES. Counting elements matching skeleton/spinner/aria-busy selectors by SELECTOR ALONE flipped public-feed from a correct pass to UNGRADED on 1 busy element at 2473 rendered characters, and did the same to engineering-design (3 at 1851) and report-sender (2 at 1176) - because pages routinely leave a skeleton node in the DOM with display:none once the real content arrives. A hidden skeleton is a template, not a loading state, so only VISIBLE busy elements count. EIGHTH, A PASSING VERDICT NAMED A MECHANISM IT HAD NOT ESTABLISHED: an unchanged page with no figures was labelled 'public-surface-identical-signed-out' and PASSED, which called project-report - a hive report page - a public surface purely because it renders no numbers in either state. Every PASS must now rest on POSITIVE evidence (a redirect, a prompt that appeared, a sentence that appeared, a stated reason for being empty); an unchanged reading and a view with no figures at all are both UNGRADED, with the reason recorded, so they stay owed rather than being banked on a label nobody proved. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: this is V1, the page as it loads, and it settles the CLIENT's behaviour when the stored session is gone. It does not test an EXPIRED-but-present token (a different path: the server refuses and the client must translate that refusal), nor a session that dies mid-action while a write is in flight. Those are separate oracles and stay owed rather than inheriting this reading. The walk is NON-WRITING - it reads, clears client-side storage in its own browser context, and reloads - so it cannot have touched the shared test database.
